newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble lower after active client demand over.
newsitem.headline: Rouble lower after active client demand over.

text.p: The rouble eased in lively trading on Friday after a pick-up in demand late on Thursday due to banks seeking funds for clients outside Moscow, dealers said.
roubles/dollar Jan 17 midday Jan 17 early Jan 16 close
"Trading started on expectations of dollar selling after yesterday's (overnight) rouble credit rise but demand did not continue today," Vozrozhdenye Bank chief dealer Maxim Poltavets said.
Dealers said banks had sought roubles for their clients outside Moscow after the New Year holiday period was over.

A Stolichny Bank dealer said banks found it attractive in early trading to sell dollars for today settlement and buy them back for tommorrow settlement, which will be Tuesday due to the U.S. Martin Luther King holiday on Monday.
Russian banks use their U.S. counterparties for settlement.
Dealers said the market, strictly controlled by the central bank, had not reacted to news the central bank would shortly consider a cut in interest rates and reserve requirements.

Central Bank first deputy chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said on Friday the bank will consider cutting interest rates in two to three weeks' time and reserve requirements in two or three months because of increased demand for funds from Russian banks.
"It is too early to see any impact, it is not that kind of market," one dealer said.
